replies.author: DohnJoe
replies.text:
Stewart Here are the logs for the Wero app

In the logs I can see:

09-04 10:34:01.537 29130 29130 E AndroidRuntime: FATAL EXCEPTION: main

09-04 10:34:01.537 29130 29130 E AndroidRuntime: Process: eu.epicompany.wero.wallet, PID: 29130

09-04 10:34:01.537 29130 29130 E AndroidRuntime: java.lang.RuntimeException: java.io.IOException: E06 (/tmp)

09-04 10:34:01.537 29130 29130 E AndroidRuntime: at . . . snip . . .

09-04 10:34:01.537 29130 29130 E AndroidRuntime: Caused by: java.io.IOException: E06 (/tmp)

Which is suggesting that somehow the app is trying to write a file in the /tmp directory and it is not allowed.

Apart the common solutions (like uninstall, and reinstall the app), I would try to check for that permission specifically.

Searching around, it seems that on Android, the temporary folder on Android should be /data/local/tmp, but this might be outdated information.

Even if the question was not pertinent, I could find developers on stackoverflow trying to access the same folder, like in this question.

So I am not sure about what is happening.

Maybe check on your File Access permission?

I do not have Wero to test it, so I am trying to have an educated guess.
